tone_statements.citation: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir. Y. Nzang Bie. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.
tone_statements.quote: Sur le plan tonal, le seki manifeste trois (3) tonèmes selon M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), à savoir : un tonème /H/ et un tonème /B/ respectivement représenté par / ʹ/ et / ˋ/. Mais aussi, un tonème descendant /D/ noté /^/. Les tonèmes ont une fonction distinctive dans la langue. La distribution des tonèmes est aisée à comprendre dans cette langue. En effet, les deux tons, H et B, apparaissent dans toutes les positions (initiale, médiane, finale) lorsqu’on élargi le spectre des oppositions au trissyllabique. Le tonème descendant quant à lui a été répertorié exclusivement en position finale des dissyllabiques /mbándzâ/ « bambou » ou dans les monosyllabiques /mbô/ « plante du pied ».
tone_statements.translation: On the tonal level, Seki shows three (3) tonemes according to M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), namely a /H/ toneme and a /L/ toneme, written with acute and grave accents respectively, and also a falling toneme /D/ written /^/. The tonemes have a distinctive function in the language. The distribution of the tonemes is easy to grasp in this language: the two tones H and L appear in all positions (initial, medial, final) when the range of oppositions is widened to trisyllables. The falling toneme, for its part, has been recorded exclusively in final position of disyllables /mbándzâ/ 'bamboo' or in monosyllables /mbô/ 'sole of the foot'.
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 (H, L, falling HL; falling restricted to final/monosyllabic position)

sources.citation: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir. Y. Nzang Bie. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.
sources.note: Section I.2.2.1 'Séki (B21)' (printed pp. 61-67) is a synchronic sketch taken second-hand from Gningah 2010: 7 vowels, 20 consonants, and (I.2.2.1.3, p. 66) three tonemes H, L, falling with distinctive function; tone patterns listed. Nothing on stress/accent for Seki. Part II (p. 237) has only a group-level B20 remark that theme-final syllables are regularly L, which 'pourrait conforter.. une évolution vers un processus accentuel' (not Seki-specific, no stress position stated).
sources.venue: Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir

tone.translation: On the tonal level, Seki shows three (3) tonemes according to M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), namely a /H/ toneme and a /L/ toneme, written with acute and grave accents respectively, and also a falling toneme /D/ written /^/. The tonemes have a distinctive function in the language. The distribution of the tonemes is easy to grasp in this language: the two tones H and L appear in all positions (initial, medial, final) when the range of oppositions is widened to trisyllables. tone.says: Seki has three tonemes with distinctive function: High /H/, Low /B/, and a falling toneme /D/ (^); H and L occur in all positions (initial, medial, final) up to trisyllables; the falling toneme is found only word-finally in disyllables (/mbándzâ/ 'bambou') or on monosyllables (/mbô/ 'plante du pied') and is rare; H predominates in monosyllables, L elsewhere; tone patterns exemplified (H+B mbélɔ̀, H+D mbándzâ, H+H ɲámɔ́, B+B dùmbù, B+H kòkú, B+B+B dìndzɛ̀lì, H+H+H mbɔ́ŋgúlú, B+H+B+H mìkálàkí, B+…
